rows: A spark gets your attention. I am interested in what keeps the room lit.
Brawling is a fire that needs air. Let me show you where the air is.
A risk is a match struck in a dark room. Make sure you know where you are standing.
Pace is the flame, not the spark. Let me choose how high it burns.
The people are the room, and I want them to feel the heat from the front row to the back.
Bottom line: I am here to light up this place, and I am not going to dim.
I want to be the headline people talk about after the lights go down.
Watch the stance light up. It is the moment before the flash.
You are big on technique. Show me one move that lights up the room, and then tell me you can repeat it.
Strikes are sparks. The question is whether you can keep the fire going after them.
A risk is worth it if the crowd can see it coming and wants to see it land.
A stall puts the room to sleep. I will not let that happen.
The people deserve a match that keeps them lit from the first bell to the last.
You call me a trend. I am a flame that keeps burning, and I can show you why.
You are proud of your {strength}. Good. It is bright. It is bright. Let me see if it lights up the whole room.
I have seen your {strength}, and I think it burns hot at the start and cools too quickly.
Steady, like a steady flame. Right, then, light it. Calm does not burn bright, but it does keep the fire from spreading.
Agreed, for now, the spark holds. We agree on what the room wants.
I could set fire to that comment. I would rather let it burn out on its own.
One fall, one spark. Keep me down, and the room will remember the spark.
On the mat, the heat is close. Stay close, and feel it.
Grounded or standing, the flame stays lit.
Keep your eyes on the flame. The room is watching, so give them something to watch.
Fine spark of an answer. The room lit up for that one.
You have not lit a reply yet. The room is waiting for the flame.
Agreed, for now, the spark holds. That is the kind of spark I want.
Fair spark, I take it. We will see how bright it burns at the bell.
I will give this match everything I have, and I will keep the room lit to the end.
My approach is bold. You will see the fire on the night.
Whatever happens, the room will remember how it looked.
The fire is not out yet. The flame is still burning.
I have one more spark, and you will see it when the bell rings.
